rationale: While multiple clinical cohorts and reviews establish that biallelic and candidate pathogenic variants in TBC1D32 cause congenital hypopituitarism commonly presenting with features of pituitary stalk interruption syndrome (PSIS) including anterior pituitary hypoplasia and ectopic posterior pituitary, the literature does not validate the quantitative claim that the classic PSIS triad occurs in over 85% of live-born individuals with biallelic variants. PSIS triads in TBC1D32 and related ciliopathies are frequently incomplete, phenotypes can manifest as isolated or non-triad pituitary hypoplasia, and heterozygous missense variants of uncertain significance have also been reported in sporadic cohorts.

evidence.text: Mutations in TBC1D32 have been linked to congenital hypopituitarism and pituitary stalk interruption syndrome, which is defined by an ectopic posterior pituitary gland, anterior pituitary hypoplasia, and an interrupted or attenuated pituitary stalk on MRI.

conflicts: The literature demonstrates that neurohypophyseal defects in congenital hypopituitarism and PSIS cohorts can be incomplete (e.g. absent stalk with orthotopic posterior pituitary, or isolated anterior hypoplasia without ectopic neurohypophysis).

Current published data do not support a strict penetrance threshold of >85% for the full structural triad exclusively in live-born individuals with biallelic TBC1D32 mutations due to small reported sample sizes and phenotypic variability.
